Package com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.picker

Class PickerExportService

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.picker.PickerExportService
public final class PickerExportService extends Object
Server-side half of /sg export (reached via PickerExportPacket): validates a client-authored eye config, writes it as canonical datapack JSON into the world's somegoogly-picker pack, and reloads datapacks as /reload does so it persists and re-syncs through the normal path. Owning this on the server is what lets a remote client export.

The payload is never trusted: the entity id must parse and exist in the entity registry (which is also the whole path-traversal defense — a valid ResourceLocation can't contain .. or escape characters, so a file path built from its components stays inside the pack), the ender dragon is refused (mirroring the reload listener's hard exclusion), and the config must decode through RuntimeConfig.CODEC — whose fields are all required, so a malformed or wrong-typed payload is rejected outright rather than decoding to an empty config — and contain at least one usable eye. The declared version is resolved from the server's loaded mod version — the one that matters for its datapack; client and server versions may legally differ (see EyeConfigModel.ConfigFile.exportVersion(java.lang.String)).

Every attempt passes the export throttles in PickerGate.tryExport(net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer, java.util.UUID) before codec work, and a success arms the longer per-player cooldown, since each one triggers a full datapack reload. Picker use is very intermittent, so the brief reload lag and waits are acceptable. All entry points run on the server thread.
